significance: A Shakta pitha on the Kushabhadra estuary about 5 km from Konark, held to be older than the Sun Temple itself. Architecturally modest, it matters as one of Odisha's well-known seats of the goddess, whom some accounts identify instead with Mayadevi, consort of Surya.
story: When the iconoclast Kalapahad came for her, the goddess is said to have met him disguised as a maidservant, asked him to wait at the door while she fetched water from the river, and escaped to the Kushabhadra, later appearing in a priest's dream to ask for a temple on its bank.
